The [[Demography|demographics]] of [[Palestine]], as defined by the [[Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics]] (PCBS), includes general [[Population (human biology)|population]] information for all [[Palestinians]], including those not residing in the [[Palestinian territories]]. As of mid-2025, there are about 
15.2 million Palestinians in the world, 7.8 million of them residing outside [[Mandatory Palestine|historic Palestine]]. Of those within the territories that comprise their historic homeland, 5.61 million Palestinians reside in the 1967 [[Palestinian territories]], and 1.9 million in the 1948 territories (now modern [[Israel]]).<ref>[https://docs.publicnow.com/viewDoc?filename=130158%5CEXT%5C7CB0BE22E446CA4D3E8D7937D03FA8C71905659D_3BBFAAE032504B19C00D58B77DCCE9818AD9D999.PDF Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS) Presents the Conditions of the Palestinian Population on the Occasion of the World Population Day]. 11/07/2025. [[Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics]].</ref> Specific information on education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects is provided by the PCBS mainly for the Palestinian territories alone.

{{Palestinians}}

According to a commonly used definition as relating to an application of the [[1949 Armistice Agreement]] [[green line (Israel)|green line]], the [[Palestinian territories]] have contributory parts of the [[Gaza Strip]] and the [[West Bank]] (including [[East Jerusalem]]).

The [[Palestinian Authority|Palestinian National Authority]], the [[United Nations Security Council]],<ref>[[UN Security Council Resolution 446|Resolution 446]], [[UN Security Council Resolution [[Israel]] refers to the administrative division encompassing Israeli-controlled Jewish-majority civilian areas of [[Area C (West Bank)|Area C]] of the West Bank, excluding East Jerusalem, as the ''[[Judea and Samaria Area]]'' ({{langx|he|אֵזוֹר יְהוּדָה וְשׁוֹמְרוֹן}}, ''Ezor Yehuda VeShomron'').<ref name=SAI2012>{{cite web|url=http://www1.cbs.gov.il/shnaton63/map/01_01e.pdf |title=Statistical Abstract of Israel 2012 |access-date=15 January 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215195555/http://www1.cbs.gov.il/shnaton63/map/01_01e.pdf |archive-date=15 December 2013 }}</ref>

===Population size and structure===
====Israeli estimates====
The [[Israel Central Bureau of Statistics]] estimated (2017) that the collective population in the Palestinian territories amounted to 4,543,126 people in 2017. Thereof, 2,155,743 Arabs live in the West Bank, 1,795,183 Arabs live in the Gaza Strip, and 391,000 Jews live in the West Bank outside of East Jerusalem.<ref name="West Bank" /> Approximately 214,600 Jews live in East Jerusalem.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Korach |first1=Michal |author2=Maya Choshen |year=2018 |title=Jerusalem: Facts and Trends 2018: The State of the City and Changing Trends |url=http://en.jerusaleminstitute.org.il/.upload/jerusalem/Jeruslaem%20Facts%20and%20Trends%202018-%202.Population.pdf |series=Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research – Publication no. 485 |location=Jerusalem |publisher=Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research |oclc=1164773453}}</ref> East Jerusalem, once administered by Jordan, came under Israeli occupation after the 1967 [[Six-Day War]].<ref>[[Ian Lustick|Ian S. Lustick]], [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230309160_Has_Israel_Annexed_East_Jerusalem/file/e0b4952793cb602277.pdf "Has Israel Annexed East Jerusalem?"], ''[[Middle East Policy]]'', Vol. V, No. 1, pp. 34–45, January 1997; accessed 25 November 2014.</ref> In the Palestinian territories, c. 86% of the population is Arab (predominantly [[Sunni Islam|Sunni]]), c. 13% is Jewish, other <1% (cf. [[Demographics of Israel|Israel]]: Jewish 74%, Arab 21%, other 5%).<ref name="West Bank" />

====US CIA estimates====
The demographic statistics of ''The World Factbook'' the 2023 estimated population of Israel including the Golan Heights and East Jerusalem is 9,043,387 (2023 est.). Of this population:<ref>{{cite web |title=Israel |url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/israel/#people-and-society |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131100823/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/israel/#people-and-society |url-status=dead |archive-date=31 January 2024 |website=The World Factbook |publisher=Central Intelligence Agency |access-date=13 February 2024 |language=en |date=31 January 2024}}</ref>
* Approximately 236,600 Israeli settlers lived in East Jerusalem (2021)
* The split by ethnoreligious groups was Jewish 73.5% (of which Israel-born 79.7%, Europe/America/Oceania-born 14.3%, Africa-born 3.9%, Asia-born 2.1%), Palestinian and other Arab non-Jews 21.1%, other 5.4% (2022 est.)
* By religion, the split was Jewish 73.5%, Muslim 18.1%, Christian 1.9%, Druze 1.6%, other 4.9% (2022 est.)

====Palestinian estimates====
According to the [[Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics]] (PCBS), the number of Palestinians in the Palestinian Territories was 3,935,249 in 2009, resulting in a calculated population density of 654 capita per km<sup>2</sup>, of which 433 capita/km<sup>2</sup> in the [[West Bank]] including Jerusalem and 4,073 capita/km<sup>2</sup> in [[Gaza Strip]].<ref name="PCBSfig09">[http://www.pcbs.gov.ps/Portals/_PCBS/Downloads/book1661.pdf Palestine in Figures 2009] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222065327/http://www.pcbs.gov.ps/Portals/_PCBS/Downloads/book1661.pdf |date=22 December 2011 }} [[Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics]], May 2010</ref> In the mid-2009, the share of population less than 15 years was 41.9% and above 65 years 3%.<ref name="PCBSfig09" />

====UN estimates====
According to the [[UN]], the population in the [[State of Palestine]] was c. 4.9 million in 2017, resulting in an estimated [[population density]] of 817 [[Per capita|capita]] per km<sup>2</sup>.<ref>{{cite web|title=State of Palestine – General Information|url=http://data.un.org/en/iso/ps.html |publisher=United Nations|access-date=8 March 2018}}</ref> However, a Census held on 1 December 2017 resulted in a total of 4,781.245. The estimate of the Palestine Central Bureau of Statistics for mid 2023 showed a population total of 5,483,450.
<!-- [dead hyperlink, cited data not found during research:] According to the [[U.S. Census]], [[population growth]] mid-1990-2008 in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] and [[West Bank]] was 106% from 1.9 million (1990) to 3.9 million persons.<ref>[https://www.census.gov/population/international/ US Census Bureau International Programs] International Data Base IDB West Bank and Gaza</ref>-->

====Reliability of data====
West Bank and Gaza population numbers appear to be unreliable, with estimates varying by a million.<ref>{{cite news |title=How Many Palestinians Live in Gaza and the West Bank? It's Complicated |url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2018-03-28/ty-article/how-many-palestinians-live-in-gaza-and-the-west-bank-its-complicated/0000017f-e074-d75c-a7ff-fcfdaa500000 |access-date=16 August 2026 |work=Haaretz |date=March 28, 2018}}</ref>

====Key derived statistics====
Out of 224 listed countries and territories, in 2018, the West Bank ranked 48th with a [[total fertility rate]] (TFR) of 3.2, and the Gaza Strip ranked 31st with a TFR of 3.97 according to ''The World Factbook''.<ref>{{cite web|title=COUNTRY COMPARISON :: TOTAL FERTILITY RATE|url=https://www.cia.gov/library/publications/the-world-factbook/rankorder/2127rank.html|website=The World Factbook|publisher=CIA|access-date=13 May 2019|archive-date=28 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091028133713/https://www.cia.gov/library/publications/the-world-factbook/rankorder/2127rank.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2018, the West Bank had an estimated [[population growth rate]] of 1.81% (country comparison to the world: 56th) and the Gaza Strip had a population growth rate of 2.25% (35th).<ref name="West Bank"/><ref name="cia_gaza"/><ref name="CIA-FB-PGR2018">{{cite web|title=COUNTRY COMPARISON :: POPULATION GROWTH RATE|url=https://www.cia.gov/library/publications/the-world-factbook/rankorder/2002rank.html#we|website=The World Fact Book|publisher=CIA|access-date=8 March 2018|archive-date=27 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160527070418/https://www.cia.gov/library/publications/the-world-factbook//rankorder/2002rank.html#we|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Demographics of the Gaza Strip==
The following demographic statistics are from ''The World Factbook'', unless otherwise indicated.

===Population===
Current:  2,098,389 (2023 est.)<ref name="cia_gaza"/>

In 2023 approximately 2.1 million Palestinians lived in the Gaza Strip,<ref name="cia_gaza"/> around 1.6 million of them UN-registered refugees.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.un.org/unrwa/refugees/gaza.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071217211906/http://www.un.org/unrwa/refugees/gaza.html|archive-date=17 December 2007 |title=UNRWA: Palestine refugees |publisher=United Nations |access-date=1 June 2010}}</ref>

===Age structure===
0–14 years: 44.1% (male 415,746/female 394,195)<br />15–24 years: 21.3% (male 197,797/female 194,112)<br />25–54 years: 28.5% (male 256,103/female 267,285)<br />55–64 years: 3.5% (male 33,413/female 30,592)<br />65 years and over: 2.6% (male 24,863/female 22,607) (2018 est.)

===Ethnic groups===
Palestinian/Arab 98.7%

===Religions===
[[Sunni Muslim]] 98–99%, [[Arab Christians]] 0.2% (2,000 to 3,000 est.), other, unaffiliated, unspecified <1.0% (2012 est.).<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/middle_east/4514822.stm Middle East Christians: Gaza pastor] BBC News, 21 December 2005</ref><ref name="cia_gaza">{{Cite web | url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/gaza-strip/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112082940/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/gaza-strip | url-status=dead | archive-date=12 January 2021 | title=Middle East :: Gaza Strip — the World Factbook – Central Intelligence Agency| date=6 June 2022}}</ref>

===Languages===
[[Arabic]] ([[Palestinian Arabic]], [[Modern Standard Arabic]]), [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] (spoken by many older Gaza Palestinians), [[English language|English]] (widely understood)

==Demographics of the West Bank==
{{Update section|date=February 2024}}

[[File:Bevölkerungspyramide Gazastreifen 2016.png|thumb|Population pyramid Gaza Strip 2016]]
[[File:Bevölkerungspyramide Westjordanland 2016.png|thumb|Population pyramid West Bank 2016]]

The following demographic statistics are from ''The World Factbook'', unless otherwise indicated.

===Population===
Total 3,243,369 (2024 est.); 71.72% of the population is Arab (predominantly Sunni), 28.28% is Jewish<ref name="West Bank">{{cite web|url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/west-bank/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106172251/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/west-bank/|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 January 2021|title=CIA – The World Factbook: West Bank|publisher=Cia.gov|access-date=2019-04-07}}</ref> (cf. [[Demographics of Israel|Israel]]: Jewish 74%, Arab 21%, other 5%; and [[Demographics of the Palestinian territories#Demographics of the Gaza Strip|Gaza]]: Arab 99%)<ref>{{cite book |chapter-url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/israel/ |chapter=Israel |title=[[The World Factbook]] |publisher=Cia.gov |access-date=2018-03-08}}</ref>

* Palestinian Arab 2,155,743 (July 2017 est.), 71.72%<ref name="West Bank" />
* Israeli Jew 850,481 (2016, 2020 est.), 28.28%<ref name="West Bank" /> 
** Approximately 475,481 Israeli Jews thereof live in the West Bank (2020)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/west-bank-settler-population-surged-during-trump-era-report-says|title=West Bank settler population surged during Trump era, report says|website=The Times of Israel|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>
** Approximately 375,000 Israeli Jews thereof live in East Jerusalem (2016)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.israelnationalnews.com/Articles/Article.aspx/18210#.VpK885scTIU|title=Settlement population growth slows for 10th straight year|date=9 January 2016 |access-date=2019-12-04}}</ref>
* Around 380 [[Samaritans]]{{efn|Samaritans in the [[West Bank]] have Palestinian citizenship. {{harv|Sabella|2011|p=75, n.4}}.}}<ref>{{cite book| chapter = The Status of Non-Muslims in a Palestinian State
 | last = Sabella | first = Bernard | year = 2011
 | title = Non-Muslims in Muslim Majority Societies: With Focus on the Middle East and Pakistan

===Ethnic groups===
Palestinian Arab: 83%<br />Israeli Jewish and other: 17%

===Religions===
Muslim 80–85% (predominantly Sunni)<br />Jewish 12–14%<br />Christian 1.0–2.5%, (mainly Greek Orthodox)<ref name="West Bank" /><br />Other religious minorities include [[Palestinian Metawalis]], [[Palestinian Druze]], and [[Palestinian Baha'is]].{{dubious|date=January 2026}}

===Languages===
[[Arabic]] ([[Palestinian Arabic]], [[Modern Standard Arabic]]), [[English language|English]] (compulsory in schools, widely{{Quantify|date=May 2019}} spoken by Palestinians), and [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] (spoken by Israeli Jews in the West Bank, and spoken by many{{Quantify|date=May 2019}} Palestinians) are commonly known.
